story: Raj drives for Uber and Lyft; a kidney stone put him in CPMC's emergency department (CT, labs, IV fluids), rebuilt from CPMC's real price file. Insured, household of 4 (his wife's part-time paychecks plus his gig payouts) at about 135% of the poverty line. The bill lists the IV hydration twice, charges the CT above CPMC's own posted price, ignores his insurance and misses the $400 he paid. His share of this bill alone is under Sutter's 10%-of-income bar; his last 12 months of medical bills in the bank (urgent care, imaging, pharmacy, physical therapy, the kids' pediatrician) put him over it, so Sutter writes his share off and the $400 comes back.
